plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following is the charging section for Income-tax in India under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
plain.explanation: Section 4 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 is the charging section which provides that income-tax shall be charged for any assessment year at the relevant rates in respect of the total income of the previous year of every person. Section 2 deals with definitions, Section 5 with scope of total income, and Section 10 with incomes not included in total income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the general rule regarding the determination of the previous year for a business newly set up on 15th November of the current financial year?
options: From 1st April of the current financial year to 31st March of the next year
From 15th November of the current financial year to 31st March of the next year
From the date of setting up to 31st December of the current financial year
From 15th November of the current financial year to 30th September of the next year
plain.explanation: As per Section 3, for a newly set-up business or profession, the first previous year begins on the date of setting up of the business or profession and ends on 31st March of the financial year. Therefore, it will be from 15th November to 31st March.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, income earned in a previous year is assessed to tax in:
options: The assessment year following the previous year
Any year chosen by the Assessing Officer
plain.explanation: The general rule under the Income-tax Act is that income earned in a previous year is taxed in the immediately following assessment year. Section 4 mandates that income-tax is charged for any assessment year on the total income of the previous year.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following represents an exception to the general rule that income of a previous year is assessed in the immediately following assessment year?
options: Income of a person leaving India permanently
Income from salary received in advance
Income of a salaried employee with multiple employers
Income from house property let out for residential purposes
plain.explanation: Sections 174 to 176 provide exceptions to the rule where income of a previous year is assessed in the same previous year itself. One such exception is the income of a person leaving India permanently with no intention of returning.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: For the purpose of Income-tax Act, 1961, the term 'Person' under Section 2(31) includes how many distinct categories?
plain.explanation: Section 2(31) defines 'person' to include 7 categories: (i) Individual, (ii) Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), (iii) Company, (iv) Firm, (v) Association of Persons (AOP) or Body of Individuals (BOI), (vi) Local authority, and (vii) Artificial juridical person.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In computing total income, which of the following deductions is allowed from Gross Total Income under Chapter VI-A?
options: Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium
Interest on borrowed capital under Section 24(b)
plain.explanation: Deductions under Chapter VI-A (such as Section 80C) are made from the Gross Total Income. Section 16 deductions are from salary income, and Section 24(b) is from house property income, before arriving at Gross Total Income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following incomes is completely exempt from income-tax under Section 10 of the Income-tax Act, 1961?
options: Capital gains from transfer of listed shares
plain.explanation: Agricultural income in India is exempt under Section 10(1). Winnings from horse races are taxable under Section 56(2)(ib) at special rates. Capital gains and director's fees are also taxable under their respective heads.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under the default tax regime (Section 115BAC) for individuals, which of the following deductions under Chapter VI-A is generally NOT available?
options: Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's contribution to NPS
Deduction under Section 80CCD(1B) for employee's contribution to NPS
Deduction under Section 80C for Provident Fund and life insurance
Deduction under Section 80JJAA for employment of new workmen
plain.explanation: Under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC, most deductions under Chapter VI-A like Section 80C, 80D, 80G, etc., are not available. However, deductions under Section 80CCD(2) and 80JJAA are permitted.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the tax status of a co-operative society under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
options: Treated as an Association of Persons (AOP)
Treated as a distinct category of 'Person' under Section 2(31)
plain.explanation: A co-operative society is specifically included as a distinct entity under 'Company' in an expanded definition or rather treated under specific tax rates, but strictly speaking, co-operative societies fall under the category of 'Local authority' or specific corporate definitions? Wait, let's check: Section 2(31) includes local authorities, but co-operative societies are legally treated as a 'Company' for income-tax rate purposes or separate entity? Actually, co-operative societies are treated as a separate category of person or under AOP? Correction: Co-operative society is treated as a separate category under Section 2(31)(vii) or as part of AOP? No, co-operative society is a co-operative society registered under Co-operative Societies Act, taxed as a separate entity (neither company nor firm nor AOP, but a distinct entity mentioned in finance acts and charging provisions). Let's review standard classification: Company, Firm, AOP/BOI, Local Authority, Artificial Juridical Person. Co-operative societies are assessed as a separate category of person.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can an assessee have different previous years for different sources of income under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
options: No, all sources of income must have the same previous year which is the financial year
Yes, if permitted by the Assessing Officer
plain.explanation: As per Section 3, the previous year is uniformly the financial year (1st April to 31st March) for all sources of income. An assessee cannot have different previous years for different sources of income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following rates are NOT prescribed by the annual Finance Act?
options: Income-tax rates for the current assessment year
Rates for deduction of tax at source (TDS) on salary
plain.explanation: Advance tax installment dates and rates are specified directly in the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 211), whereas tax rates, TDS rates on certain incomes, and surcharge rates are fixed annually by the Finance Act passed by Parliament.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: An association of persons (AOP) is formed by two non-corporate entities for a joint venture. How is the AOP taxed if the individual shares of members are indeterminate or unknown?
options: At individual slab rates of members
plain.explanation: Under Section 167B, if the shares of the members of an AOP/BOI in the income are indeterminate or unknown, tax is charged on the total income of the AOP at the maximum marginal rate (MMR).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Surcharge is levied as a percentage of:
plain.explanation: Surcharge is an additional tax levied as a specified percentage of the income-tax calculated on the total income of an assessee, when the total income exceeds specified threshold limits.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Health and Education Cess is computed at what rate on the income-tax plus surcharge?
plain.explanation: Health and Education Cess is levied at the rate of 4% on the aggregate of income-tax and applicable surcharge for all assessees under the Income-tax Act.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 115BAC, for an individual opting for the default/concessional tax regime, what is the basic exemption limit for the AY 2026-27 (assuming new slab rates)?
plain.explanation: Under the concessional tax regime of Section 115BAC for individuals (as amended in recent Finance Acts), the basic exemption limit is Rs. 3,00,000.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Marginal relief is designed to ensure that:
options: Total tax payable does not exceed the total income earned
The incremental tax liability due to surcharge does not exceed the incremental income above the threshold limit
No tax is paid by senior citizens having income below Rs. 5,00,000
Rebate under Section 87A completely eliminates tax for low-income earners
plain.explanation: Marginal relief provides that the additional amount of income-tax payable (including surcharge) on excess income over the surcharge threshold should not be greater than the actual amount of income earned in excess of that threshold.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following authorities is NOT part of the income-tax administration hierarchy under Section 116?
options: Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council)
plain.explanation: The GST Council is a constitutional body for GST governance and is not an income-tax authority under Section 116 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. CBDT, Chief Commissioners, and Assessing Officers are statutory income-tax authorities.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the legal status of circulars issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) under Section 119?
options: They are binding on the Income-tax authorities, but not on the assessees
They are binding on both the income-tax authorities and the assessees
They are advisory in nature for all parties
They are binding on assessees if beneficial to them, but not on tax authorities
plain.explanation: CBDT circulars issued under Section 119 are binding on all income-tax authorities, but they cannot override the provisions of the Act nor can they impose a burden on assessees (meaning assessees can rely on beneficial circulars, but authorities are strictly bound by them).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In case of conflict between a provision of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and an Income-tax Rule framed thereunder, which one prevails?
options: Income-tax Act prevails over the Rules
Whichever is beneficial to the assessee
The CBDT decides which one applies
plain.explanation: Rules are framed under the rule-making power of the Act (subordinate legislation). Therefore, in case of any conflict or inconsistency, the provisions of the parent statute (Income-tax Act, 1961) will always prevail over the Income-tax Rules.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 87A, what is the maximum rebate available to a resident individual under the default tax regime (Section 115BAC) for AY 2026-27?
plain.explanation: Under Section 87A for individuals opting for Section 115BAC, the maximum rebate is Rs. 25,000 (applicable when total income does not exceed Rs. 7,00,000, subject to marginal relief provisions).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following is considered 'Income' under an inclusive definition given in Section 2(24)?
options: Capital loss incurred on sale of shares
Voluntary contributions received by a trust created wholly for charitable purposes
Loan taken from a nationalized bank
plain.explanation: Section 2(24) expansively defines income to include voluntary contributions received by a trust created wholly for charitable or religious purposes. Loans, capital losses, and inherited properties are generally not considered income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When a business is discontinued, what is the tax treatment regarding the previous year of discontinuation?
options: Income of the period up to the date of discontinuation may, at the discretion of the Assessing Officer, be assessed in that same financial year
Income is always assessed in the subsequent assessment year without exception
Discontinuation has no tax impact until the next financial year ends
Income of the discontinued business is exempt
plain.explanation: Under Section 176, where any business or profession is discontinued in any assessment year, the income of the period from the expiry of the previous year up to the date of discontinuation may, at the discretion of the Assessing Officer, be charged to tax in that assessment year.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What does 'Gross Total Income' (GTI) signify under the Income-tax Act?
options: Total income computed after allowing all Chapter VI-A deductions
Aggregate of income computed under all five heads of income, after giving effect to provisions for clubbing and set-off of losses, but before Chapter VI-A deductions
Total receipts of an assessee before any deductions or exemptions
Income-tax liability before adding surcharge and cess
plain.explanation: Gross Total Income is the aggregate of income computed under the five heads of income (Salary, House Property, PGBP, Capital Gains, and Other Sources) after making adjustments for clubbing of income and set-off of losses, but before deducting Chapter VI-A deductions.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following entities is taxed at a flat rate of 30% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) under normal provisions, without slab benefits?
plain.explanation: Partnership firms and LLPs are taxable at a flat rate of 30% on their total income under normal provisions of the Income-tax Act. Individuals and HUFs enjoy slab-wise tax rates.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can agricultural income be clubbed with non-agricultural income for determining the rate of income-tax applicable to an individual (partial integration)?
options: No, agricultural income is completely separate and never considered
Yes, if non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000
Yes, for all corporate assessees as well
plain.explanation: Partial integration of agricultural income with non-agricultural income applies to individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs, and artificial juridical persons if non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit AND agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the five heads of income specified under Section 14?
plain.explanation: Section 14 categorizes all income under five heads: (1) Salaries, (2) Income from house property, (3) Profits and gains of business or profession, (4) Capital gains, and (5) Income from other sources. 'Income from Digital Assets' is a category of income, not a head of income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: For a newly formed company incorporated on 10th February of the financial year, what is the duration of its first previous year?
options: 1st April of that financial year to 31st March of the next year
10th February of that financial year to 31st March of the same financial year
10th February of that financial year to 31st March of the next year
plain.explanation: Just like any newly set-up business or newly incorporated entity, the first previous year for a company starts from the date of its incorporation (10th February) and ends on 31st March of that same financial year.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the primary objective of levying surcharge under the Income-tax Act?
options: To raise additional revenue from high-income earners (progressive taxation)
To replace the corporate tax structure
plain.explanation: Surcharge is an additional levy on higher income brackets, embodying the principle of progressive taxation where those with higher financial capacity contribute a higher effective tax percentage.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 2(7), 'Assassessee' means any person by whom any tax or other sum of money is payable under the Act. Which of the following is ALSO included in the definition of assessee?
options: A person in respect of whom proceedings under the Act have been taken for the assessment of his income
A salaried employee whose employer deducts TDS correctly with no pending liability
A foreign tourist visiting India for 5 days with zero Indian income
A retail buyer purchasing goods subject to GST
plain.explanation: An assessee includes any person by whom any tax, interest, or penalty is payable, as well as every person in respect of whom any proceeding under the Act has been taken for the assessment of his income, loss, or refund.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following constitutional provisions empowers the Parliament of India to make laws in respect of taxes on income other than agricultural income?
options: Article 246, Seventh Schedule, Union List, Entry 82
plain.explanation: Entry 82 of the Union List (List I) in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to legislate on taxes on income other than agricultural income. Entry 46 of the State List covers agricultural income taxes.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Mr. Raghav, a resident Indian aged 42, sets up a new retail garment business on 1st August 2025. During the financial year 2025-26, he earns income under various heads including business income, capital gains, and bank interest. He is evaluating whether to opt out of the default tax regime under Section 115BAC.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What will be the duration of the first previous year for Mr. Raghav's newly set-up retail garment business?
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 3, for a newly set-up business, the first previous year commences on the date of setting up of the business (1st August 2025) and ends on the last day of the financial year (31st March 2026).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: In which assessment year will the income earned by Mr. Raghav during the financial year 2025-26 normally be assessed to tax?
options: At the option of Mr. Raghav
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the general rule of Section 4, income of a previous year (FY 2025-26) is assessed to tax in the immediately following assessment year, which is AY 2026-27.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Mr. Raghav chooses to remain under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC for AY 2026-27, which of the following deductions will he generally NOT be permitted to claim?
options: Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's NPS contribution
Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium
Deduction under Section 80JJAA for new workmen
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC, general Chapter VI-A deductions such as Section 80C are disallowed, whereas Section 80CCD(2), 80JJAA, and standard deduction under Section 16(ia) are available.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under which head of income will Mr. Raghav's earnings from the retail garment business be computed?
options: Profits and gains of business or profession
linkedMcqs.explanation: Income derived from running a retail garment business falls under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession' (PGBP) pursuant to Section 28 of the Income-tax Act.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s. Apex Associates, a partnership firm, has total income of Rs. 1,02,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The firm comprises three resident partners who share profits equally. The firm is calculating its total tax liability including surcharge and cess.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the normal income-tax rate applicable to partnership firm M/s. Apex Associates under the Income-tax Act for AY 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Partnership firms (including LLPs) are taxable at a flat rate of 30% on their total income under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Since the total income of M/s. Apex Associates exceeds Rs. 1 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
linkedMcqs.explanation: For a partnership firm (domestic non-corporate entity), a surcharge of 12% is levied when total income exceeds Rs. 1 crore (and up to Rs. 10 crores).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How is Health and Education Cess calculated for M/s. Apex Associates?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Health and Education Cess is levied at 4% on the aggregate of income-tax and applicable surcharge for all categories of assessees.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Are the shares of profits received by the individual partners from M/s. Apex Associates taxable in the hands of the partners?
options: No, share of profit received from a firm is exempt under Section 10(2A) in the hands of the partners
Taxable only if total income of partner exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 10(2A), the share of profit received by a partner from a firm is exempt from tax in the partner's hands, because the firm has already paid tax on its profits.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Dr. Meera, a resident individual aged 61, earns rental income from a commercial property, salary from a university, and agricultural income from her ancestral land in Kerala amounting to Rs. 4,50,000. Her non-agricultural total income for AY 2026-27 is Rs. 9,50,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under which head of income is the rental income from Dr. Meera's commercial property taxable?
options: Profits and gains of business or profession
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rental income from property (whether residential or commercial) owned by the assessee is taxable under the head 'Income from House Property' under Section 22.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the tax treatment of Dr. Meera's agricultural income of Rs. 4,50,000 under Section 10(1)?
options: Fully taxable under Income from Other Sources
Exempt under Section 10(1), but subject to partial integration for rate purposes
Exempt and completely ignored for all tax computations
linkedMcqs.explanation: Agricultural income in India is exempt under Section 10(1). However, since her non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000, it is subject to partial integration for determining the tax rate on non-agricultural income.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the basic exemption limit applicable to Dr. Meera (aged 61) under the normal provisions (old tax regime) for AY 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the normal provisions (old tax regime), for a resident senior citizen (aged 60 years or more but less than 80 years), the basic exemption limit is Rs. 3,00,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Dr. Meera claim standard deduction against her salary income under the old tax regime?
options: No, standard deduction is only for corporate employees
Yes, standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried assessees
Yes, but only up to Rs. 10,000
Only if she opts out of Section 115BAC
linkedMcqs.explanation: Standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried taxpayers under both the old tax regime and the default tax regime.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Mr. Vikram, a resident individual, leaves India on 15th December 2025 for permanent employment abroad with no intention of returning to India in the foreseeable future. He earned substantial capital gains and other income prior to his departure during the financial year 2025-26.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which specific provision empowers the Assessing Officer to assess Mr. Vikram's income for the period up to 15th December 2025 in the same assessment year?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 174 deals with assessment of income of a person leaving India, empowering the Assessing Officer to assess the total income of such person up to the date of departure in the same assessment year.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the assessment year for the income assessed under Section 174 in Mr. Vikram's case for the period up to his departure?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 174, income of a person leaving India permanently is assessed in the same previous year/assessment year in which they leave (i.e., AY 2025-26, since departure is in FY 2025-26).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is required from Mr. Vikram before he leaves India in terms of tax clearance?
options: He must obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 where applicable
He must pay advance tax for the next 5 years in advance
He must surrender his PAN card permanently
No formalities are required if he is leaving for employment
linkedMcqs.explanation: Persons leaving India in certain circumstances (such as financial liabilities or specific categories) are required to obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 before boarding transport from India.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under the definition of 'Person' in Section 2(31), Mr. Vikram is classified as:
linkedMcqs.explanation: Mr. Vikram, being a human being, is classified as an 'Individual' under Section 2(31)(i) of the Income-tax Act.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: XYZ Ltd., a domestic company, has a total taxable income of Rs. 10,20,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The company is evaluating its tax liabilities under the normal provisions and checking the applicability of surcharge thresholds.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the base corporate tax rate for a domestic company under the normal provisions (assuming turnover conditions do not qualify it for 25%)?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act, domestic companies are generally taxable at 30% (unless specific turnover or concessional rates like Section 115BAA/115BAB apply).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Since XYZ Ltd.'s total income exceeds Rs. 10 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
linkedMcqs.explanation: For a domestic company, when total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores under normal provisions, the applicable surcharge rate is 12% (if total income is between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 10 crores, it is 7%; exceeding Rs. 10 crores, it is 12%).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is marginal relief available to XYZ Ltd. when its total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores?
options: No marginal relief is ever available to companies
Yes, marginal relief ensures that additional tax due to surcharge does not exceed income above Rs. 10 crores
Marginal relief is only available to individuals and HUFs
Marginal relief applies automatically without any computation
linkedMcqs.explanation: Marginal relief is available to companies as well when total income exceeds threshold limits (like Rs. 10 crores), ensuring the incremental tax and surcharge liability does not exceed the incremental income over the threshold.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which statutory authority enacted the rates of income-tax and surcharge for XYZ Ltd. for AY 2026-27?
options: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) via notification
The Finance Act passed by Parliament
linkedMcqs.explanation: The rates of income-tax, surcharge, and cess for any assessment year are enacted annually by the Finance Act passed by Parliament.
